data.title: rr_recording_stream_free blocks forever when connected to an unreachable gRPC endpoint after many log calls
data.body:
<!--
First look if there is already a similar bug report. If there is, upvote the issue with 👍
-->

---

### Description

**SDK version:** 0.33.0 (C/C++ API), Linux x86_64

`rr_recording_stream_free` never returns when the stream is connected to a gRPC endpoint that is not reachable, after a large number of `log` calls.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. `rr_recording_stream_new`
2. `rr_recording_stream_connect_grpc` to an endpoint that is not a reachable Rerun server, e.g. `rerun+http://app-rerun-viewer:8080/proxy` (returns immediately, no error).
3. Log ~1,000,000 Float64 scalars in a loop, each at its own `SEQUENCE` timeline point (`rr_recording_stream_set_time` + `rr_recording_stream_log`).
4. Call `rr_recording_stream_free(stream)`.

#### Observed behavior

`rr_recording_stream_free` does not return (verified by terminating with a watchdog after 60s).

#### Expected behavior

`rr_recording_stream_free` returns within a bounded time.

#### Additional data points

- With a single / small number of logged rows, `rr_recording_stream_free` returns after ~6s (gRPC "unable to connect" timeout).
- With 100,000 rows it returns; with 1,000,000 rows it hangs.
- Sending the same 1,000,000 rows via `rr_recording_stream_send_columns` instead of per-row `log` returns after ~6s and does not hang.

#### Script to reproduce C-API
```c
// Minimal working example demonstrating that `rr_recording_stream_free` blocks
// forever (despite its docstring claiming it does *not* block) when streaming
// data to a gRPC endpoint that never becomes a working Rerun server -- e.g. a
// service name like `app-rerun-viewer:8080` that does not resolve / is not a
// Rerun gRPC server.
//
// Observed behaviour (rerun 0.33):
//   * If only a *single* row is logged, `rr_recording_stream_free` returns
//     after ~6s. Bounded -- NO hang.
//   * If *many* rows are logged across many timeline points (one log() per
//     value per timeline sample), `rr_recording_stream_free` never returns.
//     THIS is the hang this program reproduces.
//   * The columnar `send_columns` path (3rd arg "columns") submits the same
//     number of logical rows in a single call. It does NOT hang:
//     `rr_recording_stream_free` returns after ~6s.
//
// The number of rows logged via the row API is what determines whether the
// hang occurs, not the byte size of any single row.
//
// Flow:
//   1. create a recording stream
//   2. connect_grpc to the endpoint (returns immediately, no error)
//   3. log NUM_ROWS scalars, each at its own timeline point
//   4. free the stream
//
// A SIGALRM watchdog fires after WATCHDOG_SECONDS so the program terminates and
// proves that `rr_recording_stream_free` never returned (exit code 42).
//
// Usage:
//   dev-rerun_free_hang                          # default hostname URL
//   dev-rerun_free_hang <rerun-grpc-url>         # point at any URL you want
//   dev-rerun_free_hang <rerun-grpc-url> <n>     # log <n> rows (default 100000)
//   dev-rerun_free_hang <rerun-grpc-url> <n> columns  # send <n> rows via the
//                                                     # columnar send_columns API

#include <rerun/c/rerun.h>

#include <signal.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define WATCHDOG_SECONDS 60
#define DEFAULT_NUM_ROWS 100000

static void check(const rr_error* error, const char* what) {
    if (error->code != RR_ERROR_CODE_OK) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] %s failed (code=%u): %s\n", what, error->code, error->description);
        exit(1);
    }
}

// Arrow release callbacks. The data we hand over is static, so releasing only
// needs to mark the structures as released (set release = NULL).
static void release_schema(struct ArrowSchema* schema) {
    schema->release = NULL;
}
static void release_array(struct ArrowArray* array) {
    array->release = NULL;
}

static void on_watchdog(int signum) {
    (void)signum;
    static const char msg[] =
        "\n[mwe] WATCHDOG: rr_recording_stream_free() is STILL blocked after the "
        "timeout -> reproduced the hang. Killing process.\n";
    write(STDERR_FILENO, msg, sizeof(msg) - 1);
    _exit(42);
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    const char* url;
    long num_rows = DEFAULT_NUM_ROWS;
    int use_columns = 0;

    if (argc > 1) {
        url = argv[1];
    } else {
        url = "rerun+http://app-rerun-viewer:8080/proxy";
    }
    if (argc > 2) {
        num_rows = strtol(argv[2], NULL, 10);
    }
    if (argc > 3 && strcmp(argv[3], "columns") == 0) {
        use_columns = 1;
    }

    fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] rerun SDK version: %s\n", rr_version_string());
    fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] using gRPC URL: %s\n", url);
    fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] logging %ld rows via %s API\n", num_rows, use_columns ? "send_columns" : "row log");

    rr_error error = {0};

    // 1. Create the recording stream.
    const rr_store_info store_info = {
        .application_id = rr_make_string("rr_free_hang_mwe"),
        .recording_id = (rr_string){0},
        .store_kind = RR_STORE_KIND_RECORDING,
    };
    const rr_recording_stream stream = rr_recording_stream_new(&store_info, true, &error);
    check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_new");

    // 2. Connect to an unavailable gRPC endpoint. This returns immediately and
    //    only validates URL syntax, not reachability.
    rr_recording_stream_connect_grpc(stream, rr_make_string(url), &error);
    check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_connect_grpc");
    fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] connect_grpc returned (no connection error, as documented)\n");

    // 3. Log many Float64 scalars, each at its own timeline point. Logging via
    //    the C API requires Arrow FFI structs.
    struct ArrowSchema schema = {
        .format = "g", // Arrow format string for float64 (double)
        .name = "item",
        .metadata = NULL,
        .flags = 0,
        .n_children = 0,
        .children = NULL,
        .dictionary = NULL,
        .release = release_schema,
        .private_data = NULL,
    };
    const rr_component_type component_type = {
        .descriptor =
            {
                .archetype = rr_make_string("rerun.archetypes.Scalars"),
                .component = rr_make_string("Scalars:scalars"),
                .component_type = rr_make_string("rerun.components.Scalar"),
            },
        .schema = schema,
    };
    const rr_component_type_handle type_handle = rr_register_component_type(component_type, &error);
    check(&error, "rr_register_component_type");

    if (use_columns) {
        // 3b. Columnar path: build a single ListArray of all scalars plus a
        //     parallel i64 time column and hand them to send_columns. This
        //     submits the same number of logical rows as the row loop in one
        //     call.
        int32_t* offsets = malloc(sizeof(int32_t) * (size_t)(num_rows + 1));
        double* col_values = malloc(sizeof(double) * (size_t)num_rows);
        int64_t* time_values = malloc(sizeof(int64_t) * (size_t)num_rows);
        if (offsets == NULL || col_values == NULL || time_values == NULL) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] allocation failed for %ld rows\n", num_rows);
            exit(1);
        }
        for (long i = 0; i < num_rows; ++i) {
            offsets[i] = (int32_t)i;
            col_values[i] = (double)i;
            time_values[i] = i;
        }
        offsets[num_rows] = (int32_t)num_rows;

        // Child float64 values array of the ListArray.
        static const void* child_buffers[2];
        child_buffers[0] = NULL; // validity
        child_buffers[1] = col_values;
        static struct ArrowArray child_array;
        child_array = (struct ArrowArray){
            .length = num_rows,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 0,
            .buffers = child_buffers,
            .children = NULL,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            .release = release_array,
            .private_data = NULL,
        };
        static struct ArrowArray* list_children[1];
        list_children[0] = &child_array;

        // Outer ListArray: one list element (a single scalar) per logical row.
        static const void* list_buffers[2];
        list_buffers[0] = NULL; // validity
        list_buffers[1] = offsets;
        struct ArrowArray list_array = {
            .length = num_rows,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 1,
            .buffers = list_buffers,
            .children = list_children,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            .release = release_array,
            .private_data = NULL,
        };

        // Time column (i64 primitive array).
        static const void* time_buffers[2];
        time_buffers[0] = NULL; // validity
        time_buffers[1] = time_values;
        struct ArrowArray time_array = {
            .length = num_rows,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 0,
            .buffers = time_buffers,
            .children = NULL,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            .release = release_array,
            .private_data = NULL,
        };

        rr_time_column time_column = {
            .timeline =
                {
                    .name = rr_make_string("step"),
                    .type = RR_TIME_TYPE_SEQUENCE,
                },
            .array = time_array,
            .sorting_status = RR_SORTING_STATUS_SORTED,
        };
        rr_component_column component_column = {
            .component_type = type_handle,
            .array = list_array,
        };
        rr_recording_stream_send_columns(
            stream, rr_make_string("scalar"), &time_column, 1, &component_column, 1, &error);
        check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_send_columns");
        fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] sent %ld rows via send_columns\n", num_rows);
    } else {
        // 3a. Row path: log many Float64 scalars, each at its own timeline
        //     point.
        static double values[1] = {42.0};
        const void* buffers[2] = {NULL /* validity bitmap */, values};
        struct ArrowArray array = {
            .length = 1,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 0,
            .buffers = buffers,
            .children = NULL,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            .release = release_array,
            .private_data = NULL,
        };
        rr_component_batch batch = {
            .component_type = type_handle,
            .array = array,
        };
        rr_data_row data_row = {
            .entity_path = rr_make_string("scalar"),
            .num_component_batches = 1,
            .component_batches = &batch,
        };

        for (long i = 0; i < num_rows; ++i) {
            values[0] = (double)i;
            rr_recording_stream_set_time(
                stream, rr_make_string("step"), RR_TIME_TYPE_SEQUENCE, i, &error);
            check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_set_time");
            // The Arrow array was "released" by the previous log call; re-arm it.
            array.release = release_array;
            batch.array = array;
            data_row.component_batches = &batch;
            rr_recording_stream_log(stream, data_row, true, &error);
            check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_log");
        }
        fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] logged %ld scalars\n", num_rows);
    }

    // 4. Arm the watchdog and free the stream. Per the docstring this should
    //    flush-but-not-block; in practice it blocks forever.
    signal(SIGALRM, on_watchdog);
    alarm(WATCHDOG_SECONDS);

    const time_t t0 = time(NULL);
    fprintf(stderr,
            "[mwe] calling rr_recording_stream_free() (watchdog: %d s)...\n",
            WATCHDOG_SECONDS);
    rr_recording_stream_free(stream);
    const time_t t1 = time(NULL);

    alarm(0);
    fprintf(stderr,
            "[mwe] rr_recording_stream_free() RETURNED after %ld s (no hang)\n",
            (long)(t1 - t0));
    return 0;
}


``` 

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
Ubuntu 26.04

**Rerun version**
 0.33.0
